NOS-DOS Game Guide
==================

LAUNCHING GAMES
---------------
Games installed via NPKG appear in the F9 launcher and are run through
NOSPLAY, which automatically applies the correct:
  - Memory profile (NOSMEM /GAME or /EMS)
  - CPU throttle level (SLOW33, SLOW477, etc.)
  - Sound Blaster environment variables

  NOSPLAY          Interactive game selector
  NOSPLAY DOOM     Launch DOOM directly
  NOSPLAY INFO DOOM  Show game profile details

INSTALLING GAMES
----------------
  NPKG INSTALL DOOM      Install DOOM Shareware
  NPKG INSTALL WOLF3D    Install Wolfenstein 3D Shareware
  NPKG INSTALL QUAKE     Install Quake Shareware
  ... etc.

  Requires: active network connection (NNET STATUS / NNET DHCP)
  Games are large (6-30 MB) -- downloads may take several minutes.

CPU THROTTLE PRESETS
--------------------
  SLOW477   ~4.77 MHz equivalent  (very old games, pre-1990)
  SLOW10    ~10 MHz equivalent    (286-era games)
  SLOW33    ~33 MHz equivalent    (386-era: DOOM, Wolf3D, Prince)
  SLOW66    ~66 MHz equivalent    (486-era: Duke3D, Quake)
  SLOW100   ~100 MHz equivalent   (Pentium-era: most 1996+ games)
  OFF       No throttle           (modern freeware, non-timing-sensitive)

Adjust live with Ctrl+Alt+KP+ / Ctrl+Alt+KP- while a game is running.
Use TCTL CALIBRATE once after first boot for accurate preset values.

GAME COMPATIBILITY NOTES
-------------------------
DOOM Shareware (1993)
  Preset: SLOW33  Memory: GAME (530KB conv + 2MB XMS)
  Notes:  Requires BLASTER env var. NOSPLAY sets this automatically.
          Save games go to C:\GAMES\DOOM\SAVE

DOOM II (1994)
  Preset: SLOW33  Memory: GAME
  Notes:  Same requirements as DOOM. Commercial version required.

Wolfenstein 3D Shareware (1992)
  Preset: SLOW33  Memory: GAME (530KB conv)
  Notes:  No XMS needed. Runs well on most 386+ settings.

Prince of Persia (1990)
  Preset: SLOW477  Memory: STD
  Notes:  VERY timing-sensitive. If animation runs too fast, increase
          the throttle level with Ctrl+Alt+KP+. TCTL CALIBRATE first.

Commander Keen 1 (1990)
  Preset: SLOW477  Memory: STD
  Notes:  Requires EGA. VGA in CGA/EGA compatibility mode works fine.

Heretic Shareware (1994)
  Preset: SLOW33  Memory: GAME (530KB conv + 4MB XMS)
  Notes:  DOOM engine derivative. Same BLASTER requirements.

Duke Nukem 3D Shareware (1996)
  Preset: SLOW66  Memory: GAME (570KB conv + 4MB XMS)
  Notes:  Build engine. Needs more conventional memory than DOOM.

Quake Shareware (1996)
  Preset: SLOW66  Memory: GAME (600KB conv + 8MB XMS)
  Notes:  The most demanding game in the package list. Requires 8MB
          XMS. May run slowly even with SLOW66; try SLOW100.

Descent Shareware (1994)
  Preset: SLOW33  Memory: EMS (550KB conv + 2MB EMS)
  Notes:  Uses EMS memory. Run NOSMEM /EMS before NOSPLAY, or let
          NOSPLAY handle it via the MemProfile=EMS setting.

Tyrian 2000 (freeware, 2004)
  Preset: OFF  Memory: STD
  Notes:  Freeware vertical shooter. No throttle needed. Runs great.

SOUND CONFIGURATION
-------------------
All games expect a Sound Blaster at the default address:
  IRQ 5, DMA 1, Address 220h (BLASTER=A220 I5 D1 T4)
  Or SB16: H5 for 16-bit DMA, T6 for type

NOS-DETECT configures the BLASTER variable in AUTOEXEC.BAT based on
the detected sound card. NOSPLAY also sets it per-game from SoundEnv=.
If sound does not work, check: TYPE C:\AUTOEXEC.BAT | FIND "BLASTER"

MEMORY TROUBLESHOOTING
-----------------------
If a game says "Not enough memory":
  1. Run NOSMEM /GAME from the command line.
  2. Then run NOSPLAY [id] manually.
  Or: NOSPLAY handles this automatically via MemProfile.

If a game requires EMS and it is not available:
  Run NOSMEM /EMS first (configures JEMMEX for EMS provision).

ADDING GAME SAVES TO THE HOST
------------------------------
Game save directories are typically:
  C:\GAMES\GAMENAME\SAVE\

Copy saves to H:\OUTBOX\ to get them onto your host:
  COPY C:\GAMES\DOOM\SAVE\*.* H:\OUTBOX\
Then run watch_outbox.py on the host to collect them.
